The description “naive empiricist” applies to John Austin in jurisprudence, not to ordinary epistemology: his account of law rests on an anachronistic model of a legal system, modeled on early-19th-century sovereign command and habit of obedience. That model is often criticized as naive because it treats law as a simple empirical fact of commands and sanctions rather than a complex normative practice.

CONFIDENCE: 85
